newsitem.title: UK: 70 pct of Brtish firms want to stay in EU - survey.
newsitem.headline: 70 pct of Brtish firms want to stay in EU - survey.

text.p: Almost three-quarters of British businesses believe the United Kingdom's economy is better off within the European Union, a survey by Reed Personnel Services showed on Monday.
Reed surveyed 533 organisations across the country and found 70 percent want to stay in the EU while 24 percent thought Britain was better off outside.
The remaining six percent were uncommitted.
Larger companies were more likely to support the idea of staying in Europe. Only 20 percent of organisations employing 5,000 people or more preferred to be outside.

A quarter of smaller companies with fewer than 500 employees, perhaps worried by the costs of the EU's Social Chapter which guarantees minimum employment rights, thought Britain was better off on its own.

Senior managers were more pro-European than middle management and support staff and the survey showed up regional differences too. The Midlands had 88 percent of businesses supporting EU membership while in the South West, 35 percent wanted out of Europe.

Across the industrial spectrum, 76 percent of manufacturing firms -- which make up most of Britain's biggest exporters to Europe -- favoured staying in the single market against only 60 percent of distribution and wholesale organisations.
